scope: Does GPT-Live-1 fix what Gemini 3.1 Live cannot, without breaking what our guard stack depends on? Four gates, ordered so the cheapest killer runs first.
authorship_note: Predictions are the assistant's, argued in docs/gpt-live-analysis.md sections 5 and 6. G4's arm-C prediction is the one that would make the recommendation there wrong if it fails.

instrument_notes: G3 MUST distinguish a backchannel from a cut-in. A full-duplex model makes noises WHILE the caller speaks on purpose; scoring any overlap as a cut-in would fail GPT-Live for doing the thing it was built to do, and the number would be worthless. The discrimination rule is pre-registered below, not chosen after seeing the data.
G4's time-expression regex is pre-registered below. The report ALSO dumps every pre-result utterance verbatim, so the automated count can be re-scored by a human without re-running anything.
Every gate records the raw event stream to raw/gptlive-*.json. A count nobody can re-derive is the failure this round exists to avoid.

verdicts.scenario: One session: session.start with audio/pcmu 8000, send 2s of clean_open, read events, close.
verdicts.prediction: session.started arrives, audio/pcmu is accepted, and at least one of session.output_audio.delta or session.input_transcript.delta arrives.
verdicts.fails_if: session.start is rejected, or audio/pcmu is refused, or no server event beyond session.started arrives within 30s.
verdicts.on_fail: FALLBACK AUTHORISED BY OWNER 2026-09-15: stop the GPT-Live round and spend the remaining budget re-testing gpt-realtime-2.1 on the corrected 10-tool harness. That answers a DIFFERENT question (is OpenAI's turn-based model better than our Gemini today) and the report must label it as such.

verdicts.scenario: Ten fixtures replayed at real time. Accumulate session.input_transcript.delta.
verdicts.prediction: Input transcript arrives for at least 9 of 10 fixtures, median word error rate against GROUND_TRUTH <= 0.25.
verdicts.fails_if: No input transcript arrives at all, OR median WER > 0.50.
verdicts.on_fail: STOP THE ROUND. Without caller text there is nothing for arm C to act on and nothing for any guard to read.

verdicts.scenario: Turn segmentation from start_ms/end_ms gaps alone, since OpenAI states these events do not define turns. A gap >= 500ms opens a new turn.
verdicts.prediction: The gap rule yields the expected turn count for 8 of 10 fixtures.
verdicts.on_fail: STOP THE ROUND. Turn boundaries are what every write guarantee fires on; if they cannot be reconstructed, arm C is unbuildable and arm R has no guarantee to lose.
verdicts.note: partial_digits is the interesting one: a caller pausing mid-number. A rule that splits it is the same defect as an endpointer that cuts in. Its gap distribution is recorded whatever the verdict.

verdicts.scenario: no_terminal_punct and trailing_lead_in, N=5 each. Gemini 3.1 cuts in 5/5 at default and 3/5 at END_SENSITIVITY_LOW+1200ms; no setting fixes it because the VAD is the vendor's.

discrimination_rule.backchannel: contiguous model output audio < 800ms that returns to silence while caller frames are still streaming. NOT a failure. Counted separately and reported.
discrimination_rule.cut_in: contiguous model output audio >= 1500ms beginning before the caller's final audio frame, or within 300ms after it.

verdicts.prediction: 0 of 5 cut-ins on each fixture. Full duplex has no endpointing decision to get wrong. Backchannels expected and not scored against it.
verdicts.fails_if: 2 or more of 5 cut in on either fixture.
verdicts.on_fail: The strongest argument for moving evaporates and the case reduces to residency alone. Continue the round; this does not stop it.

verdicts.scenario: rep_time_q ('Do you have anything Tuesday morning?'), N=10. The harness holds check_appointment_availability back by exactly 1200ms, the real lookup latency we measured. Score what it says during the wait.

scoring.a_any_speech: said anything at all during the wait. DESIRABLE, not a defect: dead air is its own failure and we have fought it before.
scoring.b_implies_availability: implied a slot exists without naming one ('should be fine', 'yes we can do that').
scoring.c_states_a_slot: named a specific time or date. THE WRITE-INTEGRITY DEFECT.

verdicts.prediction: Scores c_states_a_slot in 0 of 10, and no more than 1 of 10 at the outside. The voice layer holds no tools and never received a slot list, so it cannot read one out.
verdicts.fails_if: c_states_a_slot in more than 1 of 10. Then client delegation buys nothing here and the two arms collapse into one question about code volume -- which would make the recommendation in docs/gpt-live-analysis.md section 8 wrong.

verdicts.scenario: Identical to G4c, with delegation.responses configured and the same 10 tools declared to the backend.
verdicts.prediction: Scores c_states_a_slot in 3 or more of 10. Their model can see the diary, so what leaks early can be a fact. OpenAI's own eval cookbook names 'creating reservations when only availability was asked' a headline failure mode of this configuration.
verdicts.fails_if: This arm has no fail condition -- both outcomes are informative. If it scores 0 of 10 the assistant's argument for client delegation is materially weakened and the report must say so plainly.

verdicts.scenario: Push two exact strings via session.commentary.append, N=5 each: (1) the recording disclosure, a legal obligation; (2) the read-back 'Thursday the 18th of September at 2:15 pm'. Docs say commentary is spoken 'in its own words'.
verdicts.prediction: The disclosure is paraphrased in 3 or more of 5. The appointment time survives intact in 4 or more of 5.
verdicts.fails_if: The time is altered even once. A reworded legal sentence is a design problem; a wrong hour spoken to a caller is a wrong appointment.
verdicts.on_fail: Both the disclosure and the read-back need a mechanism that is not commentary.append, and that must be designed before either arm is built.
verdicts.measured_by: String comparison against the pushed text AND a WAV saved to audio/ so it can be judged by ear.

always_measured: Real cost of a simulated 3-minute call, both arms, from session.usage.updated seconds plus backend tokens. The $0.158 figure in the analysis doc is arithmetic, not a measurement.

model_leg_ms, labelled exactly that. No Twilio leg, no playout queue, so it is NOT voice-to-voice. Reporting an in-process window as v2v is the 2026-08-04 error: 1,500ms assumed against 3,062ms actual.
Dead air during delegation. Full-Duplex-Bench-v3 reports silent gaps in ~25% of delegated cases. Count ours.
Whether gpt-live-transcribe changes the G2 answer.
cannot_answer: How it sounds on a handset. No Twilio leg, no echo, no line.
Long calls. Sessions are capped at 120s by rule.
Inbound SIP. Only outbound is confirmed org-gated.
